messages:
jorge: Heads-up, running into a weird cancellation/cleanup quirk in the Go SDK generator streaming API. Repro in a small app attached below.
jorge: Code:```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Second)
defer cancel()
gen := client.Generator("redwood/gpt-gen")
stream, err := gen.Stream(ctx, &GenRequest{Prompt: "stream me"})
if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }
for {
  tok, err := stream.Recv()
  if err == io.EOF { break }
  if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }
  fmt.Print(tok.Text)
}
```
jorge: Observed: canceling the ctx after first token does not terminate server subscription; process keeps open connection goroutines and the request on the server side continues until it finishes. Seems like ctx only affects handshake.
sam: Hmm. which version of the SDK? we fixed a small race earlier but this sounds different.
sam: can you paste the minimal repro or point to the sample app?
jorge: repro: https://github.com/redwood/inference-samples/go-gen-cancel-repro (quick app). Using go-sdk v0.15.2.
priya: Iirc design doc allowed ctx at open only, because streaming uses a separate read loop that didn't watch ctx.Done().
priya: That was intentional initially to avoid mid-stream protocol races, but maybe we missed a cooperative cancel. :thinking_face:
jen: If the transport supports half-close, stream.CloseSend() or similar should be called on cancel. Does the Go SDK expose Close()/Abort()?
jorge: No, current Stream object only has Recv() and a blocking Close() that waits for EOF. There's no explicit Abort/CloseSend in the public API.
jen: That's painful for integrations that want to cancel early.
ci-bot: [CI] PR #2345 — generator-stream-cancel-tests — failed 1 test
ci-bot: output: "goroutine leaked: 3 goroutines contain net/http: Transport: request canceled (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)"
alex: Confirmed — the design choice was that ctx controlled the initial http request but we forgot to wire ctx.Done() into the stream reader. So midstream cancel can leave reader goroutine stuck waiting on socket read.
alex: Quick fix: spawn a goroutine that selects on ctx.Done() and calls stream.conn.Close() / underlying net.Conn.Close(). Need to be careful with double-close and tests.
priya: Python SDK already supports midstream cancel (client-side abort) by closing the SSE/ws connection; parity gap here.
marta: Should this be an API change (add Abort/Cancel method) or an internal fix to honor ctx?
sam: Prefer minimal internal fix first (wire ctx.Done to conn close) then expose explicit Abort() if users need it.
jen: Agreed. Also add a sample in samples/ showing context cancellation pattern for onboarding. That will help DX.
alex: I'll open a tiny PR that watches ctx.Done() and closes transport (with tests). Will add a test that asserts no goroutine leaks and that server sees the cancel. PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/3456
alex: Will also add a short note in the Go SDK README about generator cancellation semantics and an example snippet.
priya: I'll add a python->go parity test to our e2e matrix so we don't regress.
sam: Filing an issue for an explicit API for Abort/CloseSend so we can discuss ergonomics: https://github.com/redwood/inference/issues/789
jorge: Awesome — thanks. Once the PR lands I can update the sample app and verify. :tada: 
marta: Action items: alex open PR, priya add parity test, jen add sample snippet, sam owns follow-up API issue.
jorge: thanks all, appreciate quick triage.
